    • isInitName

      public static boolean isInitName(Name name)
      Returns true iff name is the constructor name "<init>".

      javac interns all Names in a per-compilation table, so two names from the same compilation are equal iff they are identical. Comparing against the table's pre-interned init name is a pointer comparison, whereas Name.contentEquals decodes the name's UTF-8 bytes into a fresh String on every call on byte-backed name tables (javac's default before JDK 23, and what Gradle's -XDuseUnsharedTable forces on all JDK versions).

      Parameters:
      name - a name
      Returns:
      true iff name is "<init>"

    • sameName

      public static boolean sameName(Name name, CharSequence expected)
      Returns true iff name has the same characters as expected.

      For a javac Name, this interns expected into the name's own table (cached across calls) and compares by identity, instead of Name.contentEquals, which decodes the name's UTF-8 bytes into a fresh String on every call on byte-backed name tables (javac's default before JDK 23, and what Gradle's -XDuseUnsharedTable forces on all JDK versions). Measured ~6x faster with zero allocation there, and neutral on string-backed tables.

      Only use this for a bounded set of expected strings (annotation element names, method names a checker matches against, identifiers that occur in the source). Each distinct string is interned into the compiler's name table and cached for the duration of the compilation, so unbounded or one-off probe strings would grow both. For a fixed literal, prefer the dedicated helpers (isInitName(javax.lang.model.element.Name), isThisName(javax.lang.model.element.Name), ...) when one exists.

      Parameters:
      name - a name
      expected - the expected string
      Returns:
      true iff name and expected represent the same characters

    • sameName

      public static boolean sameName(Name name1, Name name2)
      Returns true iff name1 and name2 have the same characters.

      javac interns all Names in a per-compilation table, so two javac names from the same table are equal iff they are identical; Name.contentEquals(Name) would instead decode both names' UTF-8 bytes on byte-backed name tables. Falls back to contentEquals if either name is not a javac name or the tables differ.

      Parameters:
      name1 - a name
      name2 - a name
      Returns:
      true iff name1 and name2 represent the same characters
